newsitem.title: ITALY: Ex-PM Berlusconi questioned by Italy magistrates.
newsitem.headline: Ex-PM Berlusconi questioned by Italy magistrates.

text.p: Italy's former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi was questioned on Thursday by magistrates investigating the man who brought corruption charges against him.

The media mogul and centre-right opposition leader was interviewed for about eight hours by the two magistrates, who are looking into alleged irregularities by Antonio Di Pietro, a hero in Italy for his investigations into public corruption.
Neither Berlusconi nor the magistrates made any comment when they left a paramilitary police barracks in the northern town of Brescia where the session took place.
Di Pietro had been the star of an elite group of Milan magistrates, known as the "Clean Hands" pool, which brought down Italy's political establishment in a series of graft probes beginning in 1992.
He resigned from his post as public works minister last month after the magistrates in this town near Milan opened their investigation into his activities.
Berlusconi was called in for questioning after declaring he had "chilling facts" he wanted to tell Di Pietro's investigators.

Berlusconi, who served as a centre-right prime minister for eight months in 1994, is on trial in Milan for two different corruption cases relating to his media empire which were initiated by Di Pietro and the "Clean Hands" pool.
Berlusconi, who denies the charges, has complained he is the victim of a political witch hunt.
Tax police acting on orders of the Brescia magistrates continued a series of raids of Di Pietro's property and offices of his lawyers and associates.
They said they had seized documents from his office on Wednesday at the northern university of Castellanza, where he began teaching after resigning as a magistrate two years ago.
Other raids relating to the Di Pietro investigation took place on Thursday at offices of the public works and transport ministries, Italian media reported.

Magistrates in Brescia also have brought to trial Berlusconi's brother, Paolo, and his former defence minister Cesare Previti on charges of plotting to discredit Di Pietro and force him out of his job as a magistrate. They deny the charges.

Di Pietro was called as a witness at their trial on Monday but refused to answer questions. He has said his decision to leave the "Clean Hands" pool was not political but has never fully explained his reasons.
